So in October at the age of 43 I bought my first firearm. A Glock 22 Gen 3. It has Night Sights and about a 1/2 second reset trigger with a 20 lb spring.

In December I bought my Second firearm. A Taurus Brazilia with interchangeable barrels (currently have a 22LR, 243 and 20 Gauge barrel for it).

January and February were spent learning about firearms, going to the range several times a week (most weeks) and stocking up on Ammunition.

Then March rolled around and I bought (which I picked up today) a Smith & Wesson M&P 15-22. This is one of the best AR15's on the market and is a 22 caliber with 25 round clips. It is semi-automatic but requires pull and release of the trigger. It is super light, awesome sights and has 4 picatinny rails. I also bought (will pickup next week) a Springfield Arms 1911 Compact 45 ACP with competition trigger and night sights. This bad boy retails for a shit ton.

Next month (April) I am buying a Standard Manufacturing Inc. DP-12. This is a Double Barrel 12 Gauge (16 round) semi-automatic assault shotgun. It has very little kick/recoil and can fire all 16 rounds in a few seconds. Not bad for the most state of the art Shotgun on the market. It is also insanely expensive.

I also became a Lifetime Member of the NRA this month.

Just think 6 months ago I had never owned a gun, now I am $4000+ in, own 4 (6 if you count the Taurus as 3) firearms and am already planning for the next one (the DP-12).

Any suggestions on what I should buy after I get the DP-12? I am thinking stockpiling ammo and parts after the shotgun but would consider adding more gun(s) if you guys have any valid suggestions (with reasoning).
New Gun Owner turned Gun Junkie - can't get enough!

You've got a nice collection started! I'd really recommend stockpiling ammo and parts like you thought, your guns aren't worth a damn if you can't load and repair them. When you get a nice stockpile, consider learning about reloading and building yourself a little workshop for it.

No where to build me a shop to do reloads. I have, however, made friends with an Ex-Cop turned Lawyer who lives near me and does his own reloads and has his own shop so I am going to learn from him when/if I get a place I can do it myself.
